gate: E2_PAIR_PARALLEL_V1 - do the E2 (rw:R1+R2) CPU gain and the pair-parallel wall gain survive together?
classification: FCC_N SCENARIO FAMILY - NOT THE 2/3-ATOM CERTIFICATION SCOPE
baseline: origin/master = local master = 15ae151 (merge of claude/resource-xrepro-multiatom-v1); work on local branch claude/e2-pair-parallel-v1 in the main checkout (no worktree)

pre_seal_checks.frozen_physics_diff_9dc9c2d_to_15ae151: none for exact_expression_gate_v1/{stream,common}.py, exact_expression_gate_v0/lang_iv.py, a_reference/ar2_lang2024.py, precision_pilot_a1/a2t adapters, rewrite_pilot_a3/, formula_repro_b_v0/, multiatom_parallel_v1/, xrepro_resource_v1/
pre_seal_checks.existing_evidence_diff: none for docs/active/{multiatom_parallel_v1,xrepro_resource_v1,resource_evolution_v1}/ and their result documents
pre_seal_checks.known_prior_results_disclosed: MULTIATOM_PARALLEL_V1 (laptop): SER_E2/SER_E1 CPU 0.916-0.950; PAR_E1 W6 loop speedup up to ~3.98, W3 ~2.7; PAR_E1 wins loop from N=3, end-to-end from N=4 (T=100) / N=3 (T=1000); wall x CPU optimum serial for N<=6, W4 for N 8-16, W6 for N>=24 at T=100. The combination PAR_E2 has never been run; no PAR_E2 timing exists before this seal.

question: When E2 is used inside the pair workers, do the E2 CPU gain and the parallel wall gain both survive? Measured, never predicted by multiplying the two separate ratios.
unchanged_contract: physics law, ALL pairs (no cutoff), KDK, dt 40, Ar40 mass, three-way domain obligation on every pair, rounding/readout (A1 cells), p = 128, the FCC_N initial-state rule of MULTIATOM_PARALLEL_V1 (experiments/multiatom_parallel_v1/scenarios.py, imported unchanged). Only the evaluator inside the pair workers and the schedule differ.

evaluators.E1: algebra = A2T probe Force(compiled=True) at p (the current BASE evaluator)
evaluators.E2: rw:R1+R2 = A3 RwForce(plan) constructed after iv.prec = p, exactly as the serial A3 path (experiments/multiatom_parallel_v1/run.run_serial with ev 'rw:R1+R2')

configurations.SER_E1: experiments/multiatom_parallel_v1/run.py serial algebra (imported unchanged; the repository stream.run loop with the force swapped for the pass)
configurations.PAR_E1_W3, PAR_E1_W4, PAR_E1_W6: new runner experiments/e2_pair_parallel_v1/run.py with evaluator E1 - the same algorithm as MULTIATOM PAR_W (persistent pinned spawn workers, contiguous canonical pair blocks, main reduces in canonical pair order block by block, KDK and readout in the main)
configurations.PAR_E2_W3, PAR_E2_W4, PAR_E2_W6: the same runner with evaluator E2 in every worker
configurations.W4_reason: fixed before any run: MULTIATOM found W4 the wall x CPU optimum at N 8-16 (T=100), so W4 is needed to answer the wall x CPU question for both evaluators

bit_identity_requirement: for every (horizon, N): all E1 runs (SER_E1, PAR_E1_W3/4/6, 3 repetitions) identical in outcome, completed steps, stop kind/step, the full endpoints key of all 6N components and cells; all E2 runs likewise among themselves. E1 vs E2 are different enclosure programs: their cells must be equal where both are DECIDED (endpoints may differ). SER_E1 and SER_E2 must also equal the MULTIATOM_PARALLEL_V1 laptop evidence records for the same (horizon, N) (read-only cross-run check).

scope.N_reason: 3, 4, 6 bracket the known end-to-end / wall x CPU boundaries from both sides (the designer's examples were 4, 6, 12, 24, 48; 3 is added before any run so that a boundary at N=3 is not cut off); 12, 24, 48 are the large-N points; nothing else was selected from known results
scope.order: per repetition: H100 N ascending, then H1000 N ascending; within each (horizon, N) the 8 configurations in the order [SER_E1, SER_E2, PAR_E1_W3, PAR_E2_W3, PAR_E1_W4, PAR_E2_W4, PAR_E1_W6, PAR_E2_W6] rotated by 2 x repetition (E1/E2 neighbours stay adjacent so their comparison sees the same machine state)
scope.estimated_cost_laptop: about 6,500 CPU s (cycle-counted), about 60 min wall; cap 10,800 CPU s (campaign stops at the next run boundary)

desktop.role: representative re-measurement of the boundaries after the laptop campaign
desktop.desktop_scope: N in {3, 4, 6, 12}, H100 and H1000, all 8 configurations, 3 repetitions
desktop.preconditions: Roblox closed, no other large Python/Codex job; load snapshot before start and before every (horizon, N) group

cpu_measurement: primary CPU = QueryProcessCycleTime of every process (main + workers / the serial process) divided by the cycle rate calibrated once per campaign on the campaign core (max over 3 x 20 busy loops of 50 ms), as in MULTIATOM_PARALLEL_V1 amendment 3; the tick-sampled process_time figure is kept as total_cpu_tick_s (known to be unreliable on the laptop).
load_contamination_rule: before every (horizon, N) group the campaign takes a 1 s process snapshot excluding its own process tree and the System Idle Process. The group is marked CONTAMINATED if (a) the summed CPU of all other processes >= 100 % of one logical CPU, or (b) any single other process whose name matches python / roblox / codex / node is >= 25 %. A CONTAMINATED group stays in the evidence, is checked for correctness, and is excluded from every performance number and boundary (reported separately). The same rule applies on both machines.
measurements_per_run: end-to-end wall (campaign side), ready wall (start -> workers ready), loop wall, per-step wall, total CPU (cycles) and its main / worker split, tick CPU, main breakdown (send, wait, reduce, KDK+other), per-worker busy wall, spawn wall, IPC bytes of one step, peak working set of every process, outcome / steps / stop / endpoints key / cells / initial-state digest

derived.E2_over_E1_same_W: for W in {serial, 3, 4, 6}: total CPU ratio and loop / end-to-end wall ratio
derived.par_over_ser: per evaluator: loop and end-to-end speedup, CPU ratio
derived.PAR_E2_vs_SER_E2: speedup and CPU ratio of PAR_E2_W against SER_E2
derived.combined_vs_product: actual speedup PAR_E2_W vs SER_E1 compared with the product (PAR_E1_W vs SER_E1) x (SER_E1 vs SER_E2), for loop and end-to-end wall and for CPU; reported as actual / product
derived.overhead_shares: per evaluator and W: startup share of end-to-end wall, (send + reduce + KDK) share of loop wall, (wait - max worker busy) share of loop wall, worker busy wall per step
derived.best_plan: per (horizon, N) among the 8 configurations: min end-to-end wall, min total CPU, min wall x CPU; and per evaluator the W with minimum loop wall
derived.first_N_PAR_E2_wall_min: smallest N (per horizon) at which a PAR_E2 configuration is the end-to-end wall minimum, and whether it stays so for all larger N

answers_required: does E2 raise the overhead shares
first N where PAR_E2 is wall-min
why combined differs from the product

decision_classes_for_the_designer.A: PAR_E2 wins stably -> keep as current execution candidate (later input to a small Selector V1)
decision_classes_for_the_designer.B: E2 gain disappears in parallel -> split the reason into startup / IPC / reduction / worker overhead
decision_classes_for_the_designer.C: clear W6 bottleneck -> canonical reduction or worker/main placement redesign as a separate later step

E2_gates: rerun the A3 runner refs / verify rw:R1+R2 / sympy rw:R1+R2 and the MULTIATOM new-domain containment gate (experiments/multiatom_parallel_v1/e2gate.py, unchanged) on each machine before its runs
checker: experiments/e2_pair_parallel_v1/checker.py, independent of the executor: regenerates every initial state with the MULTIATOM checker's own generator, checks completeness, bit identity per evaluator, E1/E2 cells, cross-run equality with the MULTIATOM laptop evidence, cycle-CPU consistency, affinities, worker exits and evaluator identity of every worker, block partition, CPU sanity, contamination flags re-derived from the stored snapshots
claims_forbidden: predicting the combined gain by multiplying separate ratios
laptop vs desktop absolute times as a winner
bit identity on these machines as a proof
boundaries measured here hold for other p, T, machines or scenario families
amendment_1_before_any_run: Before the code seal: (1) bit-identity smoke test (N = 6, T = 5, scratch): PAR_E2_W3 == SER_E2 and PAR_E1_W3 == SER_E1 endpoint keys, E1 vs E2 endpoints differ, cells equal. (2) integration dry run on the desktop (scratch, T = 10 - not a sealed horizon - N = 3, 4, one repetition, all 8 configurations): all DECIDED, gates PASS; both groups flagged CONTAMINATED by the sealed rule (RobloxPlayerBeta.exe 227-276 %, other processes 373-516 %), so no timing from it is used or was interpreted. (3) checker fix found by the dry run: the cross-run comparison with the MULTIATOM evidence now also requires equal T and N (the dry run compared T = 10 runs with T = 100 records).
